_comment: Authored toolchain compatibility requirements. This file states what amoebius needs;
it never states what a particular host resolved. No entry may carry an executable path,
a resolved version, a download URL, or a package/archive checksum: those are run-local
observations written to .build/toolchain/ by tools/toolchain.py and attached to the local run
evidence (repository_layout_doctrine.md section 4).
There is no 'expected on the developer host' source kind. A tool with a supported install
plan is ensured -- probed, installed when absent, resolved to an absolute path, and invoked
by it (substrate_doctrine.md section 3). What the operator must already supply is the floor
below, and nothing else (substrate_doctrine.md section 3.1).
source kinds:
managed        the tool is supplied by another resolved provider, which is asked what it
can supply, told to supply it when it has not, and then asked where it put
it. `provider` names the provider; the closed set is ghcup, playwright, and
package-manager (the floor's own package-manager root)
node-package   the tool ships inside a package.json dependency; resolution finds it in
the installed node_modules tree
github-release the tool is published as a release asset; resolution asks the project for
its current release, then materializes the asset under an ignored root
hackage        the tool is a Haskell package installed by the resolved cabal
kubernetes-release  the tool is published on dl.k8s.io behind a release channel; resolution
reads the channel, then fetches the binary and the publisher's own checksum
Every platform key in this file is the one canonical <os>-<arch> token of
tools/host_platform.py: the system's own lowercase name joined to the closed lane
architecture vocabulary (amd64 | arm64). No entry spells an architecture any other way.
The Bootstrap Coordinator acquires ghcup, kubectl, and kind on a pristine host before any
amoebius binary exists, so it reads these same authored requirements and writes its own
run-local resolution to .build/toolchain/. Every checksum it uses is the publisher's, fetched
in the same run; none is retained here.
The per-substrate floor of substrate_doctrine.md section 3.1: what only the operator can
supply, because it cannot be installed through a resolved tool. Three classes belong here
and no others -- the package-manager root, a hardware or firmware fact, and a credentialed
account. Each entry carries the remedy that clears it, so a failure is a value rather than
a crash, and the whole floor stays decidable for a substrate the running host is not.
probe kinds:
executable  the first of `paths` that is a file the invoking user can execute
present     the first of `paths` that exists; for a node that is read, never run
command     `argv` runs and exits zero
architecture  the host architecture equals `expect`
writable    the first of `paths` that exists and is writable by the invoking user
manual      nothing on this host can decide it; it is declared so it is named, not assumed

apple.required_for: every ensured tool, and the Lima frame
apple.remedy: install Homebrew from https://brew.sh; amoebius verifies the root and never installs it

apple.required_for: the fixed Metal bridge, git, and every on-host source build
apple.remedy: run xcode-select --install; full Xcode is deliberately not required
amoebius supports macOS on Apple silicon only; no other Mac architecture is offered

linux-cpu.required_for: the C libraries the compiler links, and the container engine
linux-cpu.remedy: install the distribution's package manager; amoebius verifies the root and never installs it
grant the invoking user passwordless sudo; amoebius never prompts for a password
enable virtualization in firmware, load the kvm module, and grant the invoking user write access to /dev/kvm

linux-cuda.required_for: the C libraries the compiler links, and the container engine
linux-cuda.remedy: install the distribution's package manager; amoebius verifies the root and never installs it
grant the invoking user passwordless sudo; amoebius never prompts for a password
enable virtualization in firmware, load the kvm module, and grant the invoking user write access to /dev/kvm
install the NVIDIA kernel driver; without it the host classifies as linux-cpu and the lane is never offered

windows.remedy: install App Installer from the Microsoft Store, which supplies winget

windows.required_for: the pre-binary bootstrap and every host-boundary invocation
windows.remedy: repair the Windows installation; PowerShell ships with the operating system

windows.required_for: WSL2, and therefore the whole Linux lane
windows.remedy: enable virtualization in BIOS/UEFI; no software can enable it

windows.required_for: the WSL2 feature install and the hypervisor launch setting

git.reason: cabal materializes the supernova source-repository-package through it

node.reason: the interpreter the Spago and Playwright entry points run under

npm.reason: it materializes package.json's authored development graph into the ignored build root

ghcup.reason: the provider that supplies ghc and cabal, here and on a pristine host

ghc.reason: the pre-cluster band compiles GHC2024 with quantified superclass checking

cabal.reason: multi-package projects with per-run --builddir and --store-dir isolation

kind.reason: the single-node bootstrap cluster of the pre-cluster band

kubectl.reason: the Kubernetes client every live band drives the cluster through

dhall.reason: Gate-1 typechecking of the authored schema corpus. The publisher offers no linux-arm64 asset, so that host refuses rather than running another architecture's binary

purs.reason: the browser interpreter bundle from Phase 25 on

spago.reason: PureScript build orchestration for the browser bundle

playwright.reason: the browser-driver library the Register-2 UI gates automate Chrome through, and the provider that supplies the browser itself

chromium.reason: the headless browser the Register-2 UI gates drive, supplied by the resolved driver rather than expected on the host

protoc.reason: protocol code generation for the native Pulsar client

proto_lens_protoc.reason: the protoc plugin that emits the Haskell protocol bindings

java.reason: the JVM that runs TLC for the Phase-3/4 model checks

tla2tools.reason: the TLC model checker the formal-model phases drive
